---

The [taxodist web application](https://3w6g1b-rodrigo-villa.shinyapps.io/taxodist_app/) is a [Shiny](https://shiny.posit.co/) front end to the R package. It runs the CRAN release of `taxodist` (1.1.0), so its results follow the same lineage parser and distance definitions as the packages. Lineages come from The Taxonomicon by default, or from the Open Tree Taxonomy or the NCBI Taxonomy, chosen in the settings bar (see [Taxonomic sources](sources.qmd)). The interface is available in English, Portuguese, Spanish, French, and German.

[Open the web app](https://3w6g1b-rodrigo-villa.shinyapps.io/taxodist_app/){.btn .btn-primary role="button"}

## What you can do

The app is organized in tabs, each corresponding to a common task:

| Tab | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Pairwise Distance | Distance between two taxa, with both lineages and their most recent common ancestor |
| Distance Matrix | Matrix for a list of taxa (pasted or uploaded as CSV), with a classification tree and an ordination |
| Between Groups | Distances from one group of taxa to another |
| Closest Relative | Candidates ranked by taxonomic proximity to a query taxon |
| Distinctness | Taxonomic diversity and distinctness indices of Clarke and Warwick for one or more samples |
| Community analyses | Taxonomic dissimilarity between samples (Γ+, Θ+) and standardized effect sizes (NRI, NTI); see [Community analyses](community-analyses.qmd) |
| Compare sources | How much the distances among a set of taxa change between The Taxonomicon, the Open Tree Taxonomy, and the NCBI Taxonomy; see [Taxonomic sources](sources.qmd) |
| Lineage Explorer | Full lineage of a taxon, with node ranks and clade membership checks |
| Search Database | Candidate records and numeric identifiers from The Taxonomicon |
| Coverage Check | Which names in a list are found in the selected source |
| Filter by Clade | Members of a list that belong to a given clade |
| Bundles | Upload analysis bundles to inspect them or compare two of them |

The settings bar applies to every tab: the **distance metric** (reciprocal, path length, Wu–Palmer, or rank-based), the **taxonomic source**, and an optional clade that restricts name matching. Each result includes a **resolution audit** showing how every name was matched, the source and retrieval date, and the citation of the source.

Results can be downloaded as CSV tables, PNG plots, Newick trees, and portable analysis bundles (JSON, see [Bundle format](bundle-format.qmd)), and many queries can be shared with a link that reopens them.

## Limitations

- The app is hosted on a shared [shinyapps.io](https://www.shinyapps.io/) instance. It may take a few seconds to start, and long lists are slower than in a local session because requests to each source are deliberately spaced. Lists are limited in size (for example, 50 taxa in Compare sources and 30 samples and 100 taxa in Community analyses), and the independent-swap null model of `taxo_ses()` uses at most 99 random communities.
- When The Taxonomicon cannot be reached, choose the Open Tree Taxonomy or the NCBI Taxonomy in the settings bar; names already in the app's cache still work.
- Live results depend on the current state of the selected source. For analyses that must be reproduced later, download the analysis bundle, or use the packages directly and record the package version, retrieval date, and numeric identifiers.
- For large or scripted analyses, use the [R, Python, or Julia packages](getting-started.qmd).
